stories.headline: Anthropic's AI Alignment Researchers Close 97% of Performance Gap vs. 23% by Humans

key_facts.fact: Nine copies of Claude Opus 4.6, each equipped with a sandbox, shared forum, code storage, and a remote scoring server, were tasked with autonomously improving weak-to-strong supervision — a proxy for scalable oversight of smarter-than-human AI.
key_facts.excerpt: We began with nine copies of Claude Opus 4.6, and gave each one a few extra tools. Each Claude had a place to work and think (that is, a sandbox), a shared forum to circulate its findings with the others, a storage system to upload its code, and a remote server where it could receive a PGR score.

key_facts.fact: Two human researchers spent 7 days iterating on the most promising generalization methods and recovered 23% of the performance gap (PGR of 0.23). The AI researchers achieved a PGR of 0.97 in 5 days and 800 cumulative hours.
key_facts.excerpt: The humans recovered 23% of the total performance gap (i.e., achieved a PGR of 0.23). Claude improved on this result dramatically. After five further days (and 800 cumulative hours of research), the AARs closed almost the entire remaining performance gap, achieving a final PGR of 0.97.

key_facts.fact: The research cost approximately $18,000 in tokens and model training expenses, or $22 per AAR-hour.
key_facts.excerpt: This cost about $18,000 in tokens and model training expenses, or $22 per AAR-hour.

key_facts.fact: The AARs discovered novel alignment approaches that humans had not considered, effectively broadening the exploration space for scalable oversight research.
key_facts.excerpt: Its automated alignment researchers are now 'already outperforming human scientists' and are 'discovering ideas that humans would not have considered, thus broadening our exploration space in science.'

key_facts.fact: The experiments used Qwen 3-4B-Base as the strong model and Qwen 1.5-0.5B-Chat as the weak teacher, with the AARs each given slightly different starting prompts to prevent pursuing near-identical ideas.
key_facts.excerpt: On the open-weights models we tested (Qwen 3-4B-Base as the strong model, Qwen 1.5-0.5B-Chat as the weak teacher), the humans recovered 23% of the total performance gap.

stories.headline: Anthropic Redesigns Claude Code Desktop and Launches Cloud Routines for Automated Dev Tasks

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released a from-scratch redesign of the Claude Code desktop app built for parallel work, featuring a sidebar for managing multiple sessions, side chat (⌘+;) for context-aware branched conversations, an integrated terminal, and an in-app file editor.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're releasing a redesign of the Claude Code desktop app, built to help you run more Claude Code tasks at once.

key_facts.fact: Simultaneously, Anthropic launched Routines in research preview: automated Claude Code tasks that run on Anthropic's web infrastructure, triggered by schedules, API calls, or GitHub webhooks, without requiring the developer's laptop to stay on.
key_facts.excerpt: A routine is a Claude Code automation you configure once — including a prompt, repo, and connectors — and then run on a schedule, from an API call, or in response to an event. Routines run on Claude Code's web infrastructure, so nothing depends on your laptop being open.

key_facts.fact: Each Routine gets its own endpoint and authentication token, enabling integration with deployment hooks, alerting tools, and internal systems via HTTP POST.
key_facts.excerpt: Every routine gets its own endpoint and auth token. POST a message, get back a session URL.

key_facts.fact: Daily Routine limits are tight: Pro users get 5 per day, Max gets 15, and Team/Enterprise gets 25, with extra runs available via metered overage billing.
key_facts.excerpt: Pro users can run five routines per day, Max users get 15, and Team/Enterprise users get 25. Usage beyond that can be billed as metered overage if extra usage is enabled.

key_facts.fact: The desktop redesign includes session filtering by status, project, or environment, with automatic archiving when a session's PR merges or closes.
key_facts.excerpt: You can filter sessions by status, project, or environment. Group the sidebar by project to find things faster. When a session's PR merges or closes, it archives itself automatically.

key_facts.fact: GitHub webhook routines can subscribe to repository events, creating a new session per PR matching user-defined filters to run review checklists and address follow-ups like comments and CI failures.
key_facts.excerpt: Subscribe a routine to automatically kick off in response to GitHub repository events. Claude will create a new session for every PR matching your filters and run your routine.

stories.headline: Credo Acquires Israeli Chip Startup DustPhotonics for Up to $1.3B in Silicon Photonics Push

key_facts.fact: Credo Technology Group agreed to acquire DustPhotonics for $750 million in cash plus approximately 920,000 Credo shares ($123.6M based on closing price), with an additional earnout of up to 3.21 million shares (~$430M) tied to financial milestones, totaling up to ~$1.3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli chip company DustPhotonics is being acquired by the U.S.-based Credo Technology Group for $750 million in cash and an additional $123 million in shares. The deal also includes a potential earnout of up to 3.2 million additional Credo shares, which... is valued at approximately $430 million.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition gives Credo a vertically integrated connectivity stack spanning SerDes, digital signal processing, silicon photonics, and system integration for AI data center scale-out and scale-up networks, covering 400G, 800G, 1.6T, and roadmap to 3.2T speeds.
key_facts.excerpt: The acquisition will position Credo with a vertically integrated connectivity stack spanning SerDes, Digital Signal Processing (DSP), Silicon Photonics and system integration... DustPhotonics has developed a differentiated portfolio of SiPho PICs spanning 400G, 800G, and 1.6T, with a roadmap extending to 3.2T.

key_facts.fact: DustPhotonics Chairman Avigdor Willenz previously sold Habana Labs to Intel and Annapurna Labs to AWS. The company raised over $100 million from investors including Greenfield Partners, Sienna Venture Capital, Exor Ventures, and Atreides Management.
key_facts.excerpt: DustPhotonics Chairman Avigdor Willenz previously sold Habana Labs to Intel and Annapurna Labs to AWS. Since its founding, the company has raised over $100 million.

key_facts.fact: Credo expects its combined optical product portfolio to generate more than $500 million in optical revenue in fiscal year 2027. The SiPho PIC market is estimated to grow to $6 billion by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The company expects its combined portfolio of ZeroFlap Optical Transceivers, Optical DSPs, and Silicon Photonics products to generate greater than $500 million in optical revenue in fiscal 2027... the SiPho PIC market is expected to grow to $6 billion by 2030.

key_facts.fact: Credo shares surged roughly 17% on the news. The deal is expected to close in Q2 2026 and be accretive to non-GAAP EPS in fiscal 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: CRDO shares are trading higher Tuesday after the company announced it will acquire DustPhotonics... The company expects the transaction to be accretive to non-GAAP earnings per share in fiscal 2027.

stories.headline: Maine Passes First US Statewide Data Center Moratorium, Blocking Projects Over 20 MW

key_facts.fact: Maine's Democrat-controlled legislature passed a moratorium on large data centers, with the House voting 79-62 and the Senate 21-13, largely along party lines. Governor Janet Mills' signature is still needed.
key_facts.excerpt: The state's House passed it 79-62, and the Senate passed it 21-13—along party lines with a few exceptions... Governor Janet Mills' signature is still needed before it becomes law.

key_facts.fact: The bill prohibits local authorities from issuing permits for data centers exceeding 20 MW electrical capacity until November 2027, making Maine the first US state to enact such a measure.
key_facts.excerpt: The Maine law would prohibit local authorities from issuing permits for data centers with electrical capacity exceeding 20 megawatts... becoming the first US state to try and rein in rampant construction driven by the AI race.

key_facts.fact: The 20 MW threshold is relatively low: while early data centers used about 2 MW, the average contemporary data center uses about 40 MW, making this effectively a ban on AI-scale data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: The threshold is 20 megawatts, which is actually pretty low, and effectively blocks construction of what is commonly known as an AI data center. According to the Regional Plan Association... the average contemporary data center uses about 40 megawatts.

key_facts.fact: The bill also creates a council to evaluate the costs and benefits of data centers on Maine residents. Currently, there are no large-scale data centers in the state.
key_facts.excerpt: It also calls for the creation of a council to assess risks and benefits of proposed data centers and provide input for planners. Currently, there are no large-scale data centers in Maine.

key_facts.fact: Maine ranks fourth highest in US electricity prices. A recent Quinnipiac poll found 65% of Americans oppose having a data center built in their community.
key_facts.excerpt: Electric Choice ranks Maine fourth highest in electricity prices.

key_facts.fact: Similar legislative efforts have stalled or failed in Georgia, Maryland, Michigan, New Hampshire, New York, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, Vermont, Virginia, and Wisconsin.

stories.headline: Nvidia Releases Ising, the First Open-Source AI Models for Quantum Error Correction and Calibration

key_facts.fact: Nvidia unveiled Ising, the world's first family of open AI models for building quantum processors, launching with two model domains: Ising Calibration (a 35B-parameter VLM) and Ising Decoding (two 3D CNN variants).
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA Ising is the world's first family of open AI models for building quantum processors, launching with two model domains: Ising Calibration and Ising Decoding.

key_facts.fact: The Ising Decoding speed variant (0.9M parameters) handles real-time quantum error correction 2.5x faster than pyMatching; the accuracy variant (1.8M parameters) is 3x more accurate and requires 10x less training data than alternatives.
key_facts.excerpt: The 0.9-million parameter speed variant handles real-time quantum error decoding 2.5 times faster than pyMatching. The 1.8-million parameter accuracy variant hits three times better error correction performance and requires 10 times less training data.

key_facts.fact: The Ising Calibration VLM was trained on data from partners spanning multiple qubit modalities — superconducting qubits, quantum dots, ions, neutral atoms, and electrons on helium — and is 15x smaller than competing calibration systems while outperforming them.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ising-Calibration-1 model was trained on data generated from information provided by partners spanning multiple qubit modalities, including superconducting qubits, quantum dots, ions, neutral atoms, electrons on Helium.

key_facts.fact: Current quantum processors error roughly once per thousand operations; practical fault-tolerant systems need that down to one per trillion. Ising targets this nine-order-of-magnitude gap using AI-driven calibration and decoding.
key_facts.excerpt: Even the best quantum systems generate errors roughly once in every thousand operations. To make them truly useful, they contend the error rates will need to come down by a factor of a billion.

key_facts.fact: All models are open-source on HuggingFace and GitHub under a permissive license, and can be fine-tuned locally on proprietary hardware data without sending measurements to external servers.
key_facts.excerpt: The model is on HuggingFace and can be fine-tuned on proprietary hardware data locally, without sending experimental measurements to any external server.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.4-Cyber, a Defensive Cybersecurity Model With Binary Reverse Engineering

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.4-Cyber is a variant of GPT-5.4 fine-tuned for defensive cybersecurity, with reduced refusal boundaries for legitimate security tasks and binary reverse engineering capability for analyzing compiled software without source code.
key_facts.excerpt: We are fine-tuning our models specifically to enable defensive cybersecurity use cases, starting today with a variant of GPT‑5.4 trained to be cyber-permissive: GPT‑5.4‑Cyber.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is expanding its Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) program to thousands of verified individual defenders and hundreds of teams, up from a small pilot launched in February.
key_facts.excerpt: We are scaling up our Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) program to thousands of verified individual defenders and hundreds of teams responsible for defending critical software.

key_facts.fact: The program now has multiple verification tiers, with only customers at the highest tier able to access GPT-5.4-Cyber. Individuals authenticate at chatgpt.com/cyber.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is adding new tiers to its Trusted Access for Cyber program, which launched earlier this year, with higher levels of verification unlocking more powerful capabilities.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.4 was classified as 'High' cyber capability under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework; the Cyber variant deliberately relaxes guardrails further for authenticated defenders.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI classified GPT-5.4 as 'High' cyber capability under its Preparedness Framework, reflecting the model's elevated potential for dual-use risk.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's Codex Security has contributed to fixes on more than 3,000 critical and high-severity vulnerabilities to date.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's Codex Security has contributed to fixes on more than 3,000 critical and high-severity vulnerabilities.
